notes: Capitulum (pseudanthium) of florets on a common receptacle within an involucre of phyllaries. Disc florets actinomorphic, tubular, 5-lobed; ray and ligulate florets zygomorphic, strap-shaped. Calyx reduced to a pappus. Seen face on the head reads as one open radial flower.

Papilionoideae (most genera): zygomorphic papilionaceous corolla, banner, wings and a keel of two apically connate petals, in racemes. Caesalpinioideae s.l.: weakly zygomorphic, open, petals free. Mimosoid clade: small actinomorphic flowers with fused corollas in globose heads or spikes, made showy by long stamens.

Three petaloid sepals and three petals, one petal a labellum, usually resupinate; column of fused stamens and style. Spurred labella (Platanthera, Habenaria, Angraecum) and hooded dorsal sepals (Pterostylis, Corybas) are common.

Florets reduced to lodicules, stamens and gynoecium, enclosed by lemma and palea, in spikelets subtended by glumes; spikelets in spikes, racemes or panicles. Wind pollinated. Symmetry, form and merosity do not apply.
Opposite stipulate leaves; corolla sympetalous, 4- or 5-lobed, salverform, funnelform or rotate; inferior ovary. Heads in Cephalanthus, Nauclea, Morinda.

Compound (sometimes simple) umbels of small 5-merous flowers, petals free, often inflexed; outer flowers of the umbel sometimes zygomorphic with enlarged outer petals (Daucus, Heracleum). Eryngium has heads of sessile flowers.
Four free clawed petals in a cross, four sepals, tetradynamous stamens; ebracteate racemes elongating in fruit. Technically disymmetric; Iberis and Teesdalia are zygomorphic.
Corolla sympetalous, 5-lobed, contorted in bud, salverform or funnelform. Asclepiadoideae (milkweeds): umbelliform cymes, gynostegium with a conspicuous corona.

Square stems, opposite leaves; flowers in verticillasters forming spike-like thyrses; corolla bilabiate (2 upper lobes, 3 lower), the upper lip often hooded (Salvia, Lamium); Mentha and some others nearly actinomorphic and 4-lobed.
Five free petals (basally adnate to the staminal column in Malvoideae), often an epicalyx; monadelphous stamens. Byttnerioideae and Sterculioideae include apetalous and small-flowered genera.
Solitary flowers from areoles with many spirally arranged tepals grading from sepaloid to petaloid, many stamens, inferior ovary within a hypanthium; zygomorphic in Schlumbergera and Cleistocactus.
Scorpioid (coiled) cymes; corolla sympetalous, 5-lobed, often with faucal scales in the throat; Echium zygomorphic.
Monocots with six tepals in two similar whorls; racemes (Hyacinthoideae, Agavoideae) or umbels (Brodiaeoideae); Muscari urceolate, Hyacinthus tubular-bell.
Corolla sympetalous, urceolate or campanulate in Vaccinioideae and Ericoideae, open and slightly zygomorphic in Rhododendron; poricidal anthers.
Small flowers with five dry or scarious tepals and no petals, often with scarious bracts (showy in Gomphrena, Celosia, Ptilotus); includes the chenopods with green reduced flowers.
Five free petals on a hypanthium, many stamens; cymes, corymbs and racemes. Doubled garden forms have many petals; Alchemilla and Sanguisorba are apetalous.
Opposite leaves; flowers in bracteate spikes, the bracts often showy (Justicia, Aphelandra, Pachystachys); corolla sympetalous, bilabiate or nearly regular.
Four or five free petals (calyptrate in Eucalyptus) and many conspicuous stamens; bottlebrush spikes in Callistemon and Melaleuca.
Succulents with daisy-like flowers whose many narrow 'petals' are petaloid staminodes; true petals absent.
Gland-dotted aromatic leaves; flowers 4- or 5-merous with free petals and a nectar disc; Correa has a fused tubular corolla, Dictamnus is zygomorphic.
Corolla sympetalous, 5-lobed, tubular to campanulate, usually zygomorphic; Saintpaulia and Ramonda are nearly actinomorphic and open.
Five free, often clawed and notched petals; dichasial cymes; swollen nodes and opposite leaves; Silene and Dianthus have a tubular calyx and coronal scales.

The broad APG family: Antirrhinum and Linaria personate and spurred, Penstemon and Digitalis tubular-bilabiate, Veronica 4-lobed and nearly rotate, Plantago wind pollinated with reduced 4-merous flowers in spikes.

Euphorbia: cyathium, a cup-like involucre with nectar glands (often with petaloid appendages or showy bracts) around one naked female and several reduced male flowers. Other genera have small unisexual flowers, often apetalous.
Acrodromous leaf venation; 4- or 5-merous flowers with free petals and conspicuous, often geniculate, poricidal stamens (androecium zygomorphic).
Parasites and hemiparasites; corolla bilabiate; Pedicularis with a hooded galea; Castilleja made showy by coloured bracts.
Campanuloideae: actinomorphic campanulate or rotate corollas; Lobelioideae: zygomorphic, resupinate, split two-lipped corollas.
Corolla sympetalous, 5-lobed, plicate; rotate in Solanum (anthers in a cone), tubular-funnelform in Nicotiana, Datura and Petunia, campanulate in Physalis; Schizanthus zygomorphic.
Six tepals, three stamens, inferior ovary; Iris with petaloid style branches; Gladiolus and Watsonia zygomorphic and tubular.
Mostly trees and lianas; large sympetalous, 5-lobed, tubular-campanulate, weakly two-lipped corollas.
Umbels subtended by spathe bracts; six tepals; Narcissus with a corona; Allioideae (onions) with small open or bell-shaped flowers.
Inflorescence a spadix of minute flowers subtended by a spathe, often coloured (Anthurium, Zantedeschia, Arum); Lemnoideae reduced. Individual flower characters are not visible in photos.
Sedges: flowers subtended by single glumes in spikelets; perianth absent or of bristles; wind pollinated. Rhynchospora colorata has white bracts.
Palms: large branched inflorescences of small 3-merous flowers with sepals and petals, often unisexual.
Corolla sympetalous, 4- or 5-lobed, contorted in bud, often with plicae between the lobes (Gentiana); Halenia spurred.
Tendrillar vines; unisexual 5-merous flowers with a sympetalous rotate or campanulate corolla.

Four tepals forming a tube that splits, the style presented as a pollen presenter; Grevillea and Banksia in racemes and spikes; Protea in heads of flowers surrounded by showy involucral bracts (a head of flowers, not a capitulum of florets in the Asteraceae sense).
Small 4- or 5-merous flowers, often with a nectar disc; Acer frequently with reduced, greenish flowers; Aesculus zygomorphic.
Rosette monocots; three sepals, three petals; inflorescences made showy mainly by brightly coloured bracts.
Many free parts, spirally arranged; in many genera the showy parts are sepals (Anemone, Clematis, Aquilegia); zygomorphic in Aconitum (hooded) and Delphinium (spurred); Aquilegia petals spurred.
Ocreae at the nodes; small flowers with 5 or 6 tepals, often in dense spikes (Persicaria) or panicles; Rumex wind pollinated.
The narrow APG family: Verbascum nearly rotate and weakly zygomorphic, Buddleja actinomorphic and tubular-salverform, Diascia and Nemesia spurred and two-lipped.
Aerial hemiparasites; brightly coloured long tubular flowers that split into 4-6 lobes, bird pollinated.
Papaveroideae: four (or six) free, crumpled petals, many stamens, two caducous sepals. Fumarioideae: disymmetric (Dicentra) or zygomorphic and spurred (Corydalis, Fumaria).
Small greenish or whitish 4- or 5-merous flowers with a conspicuous nectar disc.
Twining vines; corolla sympetalous, plicate, funnelform (morning glories) or rotate.
Four free petals on a floral tube atop an inferior ovary; Fuchsia pendant and tubular; Clarkia and Epilobium weakly zygomorphic in some species.
Spikes or dense head-like spikes (Lantana, Verbena) of small salverform, weakly two-lipped flowers.
The broad APG family: corolla sympetalous, 5-lobed; Primula salverform in umbels; Lysimachia rotate; Cyclamen reflexed.
Six large free tepals, six stamens, superior ovary: Lilium, Tulipa, Erythronium, Calochortus, Fritillaria (bell).
Unisexual flowers with petaloid tepals, male usually 4 (2 large, 2 small), female 2-5, with a winged inferior ovary.
Gingers: a showy labellum of fused staminodes, one fertile stamen; inflorescences often cone-like with coloured bracts (Curcuma, Zingiber).
Five free petals, the lowest spurred; tropical genera (Hybanthus) also zygomorphic, Hymenanthera actinomorphic.
Five free petals, beaked fruit; Pelargonium zygomorphic with a nectar spur fused to the pedicel (not visible).
Opposite leaves; corolla sympetalous, usually 4-lobed (Jasminum 5-9), two stamens; Fraxinus apetalous and wind pollinated.
Leaf succulents; cymes of 4- or 5-merous flowers, petals free (Sedum) or fused into a tube (Kalanchoe, Cotyledon).
Three sepals and two whorls of three thick petals; many spirally arranged stamens and carpels.
Five clawed, fringed petals, one differing (the flag); paired oil glands on the calyx.
Passiflora: five sepals and five petals, often similar, with a conspicuous filamentous corona and an androgynophore.
Crumpled free petals on a floral tube; Lythrum 6-merous; Cuphea zygomorphic and tubular.
Two sepals and usually five free petals (more in Lewisia).
Corolla sympetalous, 5-lobed, contorted in bud; Phlox salverform; Ipomopsis tubular; Polemonium bell-shaped.
Corymbs of small fertile flowers, often ringed by sterile flowers with enlarged petaloid sepals (Hydrangea).
Three green sepals and three petals, often ephemeral; Commelina zygomorphic with one reduced petal.
